2607.06495.title: Pitwall: Faithful Natural-Language Race-Strategy Briefings from a Calibrated Real-Time Monte Carlo Engine
2607.06495.paper_summary: Live sports commentary is grounded generation under a deadline: statements concern real, named athletes, the grounding state changes every few seconds, and no reference text exists at generation time. We present Pitwall, a production system that generates natural-language Formula 1 strategy briefings in English, Spanish, and Portuguese, treating faithfulness as an architectural property rather than an aspiration: every published sentence is decomposed into typed factual claims (positions, gaps, tyres, pace, overtakes, race control) and each claim is verified against the probabilistic race state that prompted it. The same verifier gates the fine-tuning data: of 3,045 model-written targets, only the 81.9% whose every claim is state-supported are retained, the rest falling back to a provably faithful template, so the generator never sees an ungrounded target. Verification is meaningful because of the grounding substrate: a vectorized Monte Carlo engine (N=2,000 per-lap race continuations) calibrated on 126 races (2018-2024) and validated on fully held-out 2025-2026 seasons (winner-in-top-3 90.3% over 155 backtests; held-out Brier 0.0745). A recurring finding spans both halves of the system: virtues trade off and must be gated separately. In simulation, calibration-optimal is not decision-optimal; in generation, fine-tuning on richer targets buys vividness that collapses into hallucination when the grounding state is sparse -- a failure a four-base replication traces to base-model instruction adherence, not scale, and that sparse-context auditing removes from the production model. End-to-end operation -- live timing to verified trilingual briefings -- was confirmed at two consecutive live Grands Prix (Austria and Britain, 2026); at Silverstone a timestamped probability trace, committed to disk before the outcome was known, locked onto the eventual winner ten laps before the flag.
2607.06495.paper_summary_zh: 現場體育評論是在截止日期下的基礎生成：陳述涉及真實的、具名的運動員，基礎狀態每幾秒鐘就會變化，並且在生成時不存在參考文本。我們提出了Pitwall，一個生成自然語言的Formula 1策略簡報的生產系統，支持英語、西班牙語和葡萄牙語，將忠實性視為一種架構屬性而非一種期望：每個發佈的句子都被分解為類型化的事實主張（位置、差距、輪胎、速度、超車、賽事控制），每個主張都根據促使它的概率賽事狀態進行驗證。同一驗證器控制著微調數據：在3,045個模型生成的目標中，只有81.9%每個主張都有狀態支持被保留，其餘的則退回到可證明的忠實模板，因此生成器從未見過無基礎的目標。驗證之所以有意義，是因為基礎底層：一個向量化的蒙特卡羅引擎（每圈賽事延續N=2,000）在126場比賽（2018-2024）上進行了校準，並在完全保留的2025-2026賽季上進行了驗證（155次回測中，前三名獲勝者的準確率為90.3%；保留的Brier為0.0745）。一個反覆出現的發現貫穿系統的兩個部分：優點之間存在權衡，必須分開控制。在模擬中，最佳校準並不等於最佳決策；在生成中，對更豐富目標的微調帶來的生動性在基礎狀態稀疏時會崩潰成幻覺——這一失敗源於四基準複製追溯到基礎模型指令的遵循，而非規模，且該稀疏上下文審計將其從生產模型中移除。端到端操作——從實時計時到經過驗證的三語簡報——在兩場連續的現場大獎賽（奧地利和英國，2026）中得到了確認；在銀石賽道，一個帶時間戳的概率追蹤在結果已知之前被寫入磁碟，並在十圈之前鎖定了最終獲勝者。
2607.06495.author: Juan S. Santillana et.al.
